accuracy.reason: All nine objectives match the primary CAP model: partitioned communication, real-time single-copy order, eventual operation completion rather than error/uptime, information-barrier proof, scoped majority behavior, reconciliation and conditional convergence. No global product classification is invented.

evidence.quote: Linearizability: operations behave as if they take effect in a single order that respects real time.

mechanisms.reason: The completed 12 write versus isolated 10 reader derives the impossibility, including blocking the writer and failed guessing. Majority versus isolated server explains selective progress; divergent writes explain reconciliation and possible lost intent.

evidence.quote: Guessing the new value cannot guarantee correctness across possible unseen writes.

coherence.reason: Scope, partition, consistency and availability definitions precede the proof and CP/AP/convergence consequences, followed by operation-level choices. Inspected diagrams show running disconnected servers, completed write versus old state, and explicitly majority-based agreement.

evidence.quote: Servers on both sides can still be running and receiving requests.

decisions.reason: The learner can choose strict versus stale-tolerant operations, explain client-visible waits/errors/staleness, and require a conflict policy after communication resumes. Normal latency/capacity/cost remain separate decisions.

evidence.quote: Outside partitions, CAP does not force a choice between consistency and availability.

clarity.reason: Terms are defined before use and the simple value example directly explains the obstacle. The short quorum example is scoped to a majority agreement protocol, rather than claiming counts alone suffice. UI code/diagram inspection only.

evidence.quote: Convergence means agreement on a resulting state.

outcomes.reason: Learner defines communicating copies, partition-conditioned impossibility, live/reachable separated nodes and partition-tolerance limits, rejecting choose-any-two and avoidance-by-omission.
Learner gives real-time valid order, completed-write visibility and overlaps, distinguishes eventual/ACID meanings, and explains eventual successful completion without latency or uptime equivalence.
Learner transfers the proof to values 0/1 and explains old return, refusal/indefinite wait and indistinguishable unseen-write guessing.
Learner covers safe subset progress, affected failures/delays, majority example, stale local reads, divergent writes and explicit reconciliation without intent/invariant guarantees.

Learner conditions convergence on stopped updates and resumed propagation/reconciliation, disclaims deadline/read-your-writes/intent preservation, and compares strict/stale operations and recovery at operation/configuration scope. A concrete configuration procedure is outside the contract.

sourceChecks.claim: Live inspected Gilbert/Lynch original paper definitions and impossibility proof: no atomic available read/write object across lost communication.
Live inspected original paper partition model: arbitrarily lost inter-component messages; this is distinct from all nodes stopping.
Live inspected original paper atomic-object definition: one real-time-respecting order, later reads see completed writes or later updates. Overlaps are governed by valid single-copy order.
Live inspected original paper availability definition and proof: non-failing-node operations terminate without bounded latency and reads return a value, not an error substitute.
Live inspected original proof construction: isolated second component cannot distinguish a prior remote write from no write, forcing an incorrect old return under availability.
Live inspected Raft original paper majority communication and log-commit rules. Two of three can form the required majority; one isolated server cannot commit alone under that protocol.

Live inspected Eric Brewer original authored retrospective partition recovery: divergent histories need merging, selection or human resolution; recovery must address violated invariants and externalized effects.

Live DynamoDB read-consistency documentation distinguishes eventual versus optional strong reads and temporary older values; Brewer recovery discussion supports conditional convergence and conflict-policy dependence.

Live Brewer retrospective operations/invariants discussion supports operation-level restrictions and recovery choices. Original CAP paper scopes the impossibility to communication failures rather than healthy performance/cost.
